name: Red Oxide
lede: Red oxide is a generic name for red iron-oxide earths, the red iron-oxide earths, and the books also use it for several other red minerals.

sections.title: Which oxide
sections.body: Paterson says jeweller's rouge is a powdered red oxide used to polish gold and silver, also called crocus Martis, colcothar and [[venetian-red]] [1]. Older writers used the phrase for other metals: cuprite is sometimes called red oxide of copper [2], and Gage notes that the Italian word *minio* referred to red oxide of lead [3]. The phrase on its own is a family name, not a single pigment [1][2][3].

sections.title: Earth reds
sections.body: The Pigment Compendium quotes a 1626 patent covering the burnt ochre dug in the Forest of Dean, called Spanish brown [4]. In New Mexico, the santeros collected a red oxide known as almagre from a cave above Questa, and the author who examined the mine says it was worked in prehistoric times [4]. Related names include [[indian-red]], [[english-red]] and [[tuscan-red]].

sections.title: A word of caution
sections.body: Because the label spans iron, copper and lead, never assume a red oxide is iron. Red oxide of lead is a different material from the iron earths: it is minium [3]. Red oxide of copper is cuprite, a mineral that also colored ancient glass [2]. When a recipe or label says red oxide, check the date and the metal before comparing it with a swatch [1][2][3]. The color name here follows the iron sense, since iron oxide is what the swatch resembles [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our name graph records this swatch from Maerz and Paul in 1930 [5]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings it appears in 1,187 paintings, 4.99 per cent, or 996 by the within-painting measure [6]. It is more common than 90 per cent of the named colors and peaks in the 1400s, in 78 of 945 paintings, 8.3 per cent, or 2.2 times the expected rate [6]. In 83 per cent of the 996 paintings it plays an accent [6]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [6].
